{"decision": "APPLY", "workflow_yaml": "name: Test

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container: uber/web-base-image:16.15.0-buster
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Cache yarn dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/yarn
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-yarn-${{ hashFiles('**/yarn.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-yarn-
      - run: yarn install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: yarn lint
      - run: yarn flow-check
      - run: yarn test", "rationale": "The workflow runs `yarn install --frozen-lockfile` on every push and pull request with no dependency cache, so repeated dependency fetching is measurable and the lockfile can serve as a cache input. Pattern P-LIT-GHA-CACHE (cache dependency downloads) is supported by literature evidence (S01, sections 4.2.1/Table 4) reporting modest VM-time reduction, with preconditions met: repeated dependency fetching exists and cache inputs include the lockfile. No equivalent cache already exists, and no contraindication applies (no mutable/untrusted cached content). All existing steps (lint, flow-check, test) are preserved unchanged, so build and test coverage is intact.", "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]}
